title: A Collection of Complaints About AI 3D Tools：We Need Your Feedback
author: Maggiedhm
selftext:
I'm looking for honest, critical feedback on how AI 3D tools perform in real world scenarios.

If you use AI models in gaming, animation, or 3D-printed models, I really need some candid feedback right now:

1. In what areas do current AI models fall short?
2. Is it topology, polygon count, UVs, textures, materials, proportions, skeleton binding, style control, or something else (feel free to use technical terms)?
3. Would they be usable if these issues were fixed? What are your honest thoughts on AI modeling tools (do you dislike them, accept them, or hope they'll improve)?
4. Which AI models have you tried?
5. What problems do you hope AI models will solve?

Please be transparent and follow the community guidelines.

I'm especially hoping for direct, constructive feedback.

Thank you—I'll be online to respond to comments at any time.

comments.author: ArS-13
comments.body:
So I just played with all the 3d model tools but it you don't want to pay for a subscription that's going up be quite limited in what you can test... Because most tools don't let you download something and therefore it's hard to tell what you can really do with the models.

Don't get me wrong many tools offer you a free or at least some limited free generations but only a few let you download maybe one model. 

But there's one tool which I can recommend for anyone low on budget: tencent global. You have daily tokens and can download whatever you generated. That's a solid option for any one trying 3d gen ai. But there's always a catch the models are off course limited and not super duper detailed but I mostly created files for 3d printing. So I wanted a slightly comic styled look for clear tabletop prints. 

One good thing is if you can generate an object from multiple views, sadly for very detailed models nano banana will fail you but usually you get a good front and back view. Everything that's concluded will often not be generated: as an example I once made a merfolk knight with a big shield made from sea shells... But the arm behind the shield never was created.

This brings us to what you should learn if you want to make something really cool and you know what kind of design you need: separate your model beforehand and use tools like blender to arrange everything back together... Or generate the same object like three times and then start to Frankenstein.

Overall I'm not a pro and you probably can get very cool and detailed results from modern tools but if you want to stay cheap you still have great options.
